name: security-oidc-issuer-discovery-review
intent: OIDC discovery metadata and issuer selection trust
artifacts: Discovery/registration flow, tenant-to-issuer registry, metadata cache, key retrieval and callback issuer validation.
trace: Follow who selects issuer metadata and where its issuer, endpoints and keys become trusted. Keep owned discovery fixtures separate from arbitrary external fetch probing.
experiment: Use two owned issuers with distinct keys and subjects; compare the configured issuer with metadata or callback from the other issuer.
disproof: Fetching public metadata is normal; a discovered URL alone does not prove SSRF or login mix-up.
repair: Pin issuer/client context through discovery, caching and callback validation; verify legitimate tenant onboarding and cross-issuer rejection.
branch_decisions: Keep configured issuer identity stable across metadata caching and endpoint/key selection. Supporting several tenants is legitimate if each authorization transaction retains its issuer/client binding. A metadata fetch that merely redirects or fails is not a demonstrated login mix-up or server fetch authority violation.
operational_method: Compare the configured expected issuer and returned iss using the selected OIDC exact issuer rules; do not normalize away a path, case-sensitive component or trailing slash as a convenience. Record discovery/key cache keys and the authorization transaction issuer. Two owned issuers with similar metadata URLs or colliding tenant cache entries distinguish metadata availability from a trust substitution.
